title: Auditor PASS/WARN + EGPS red => cycle FAIL with no reconciliation or surfaced conflict
notes: Cycle-1116 auditor verdict PASS, cycle-1107 WARN ('the work is correct, green and honestly reported'), cycle-1117 'Not FAIL, because the trade is net-positive' — all three shipped a FAIL because EGPS red_count>0. The deterministic gate SHOULD outrank prose, so failing closed is defensible; what is not defensible is that the conflict is invisible: nothing records 'agent said PASS, gate said RED', so an operator reading the dossier cannot tell a real defect from a poisoned predicate. Emit an explicit verdict-conflict record (agent verdict, gate verdict, the red ids) and treat a PASS/WARN-vs-RED disagreement as a first-class signal that the PREDICATE may be at fault — that is exactly what audit-probe-tree-isolation turned out to be. RECURRENCE CONTEXT: this is the 4th instance of a named family — lessons cycle-87-audit-vs-egps-verdict-divergence (conf 0.92, prescribed 4 fixes), cycle-352-egps-cannot-honor-auditor-false-red-adjudication (0.95), cycle-456-coverage-predicate-race-nonhermetic-flips-gating-verdict (0.9). All four cycle-87 fixes are grep-verified ABSENT at HEAD (no exempt enum, no gate_audit_to_retrospective, no exemption parser; ShipEligible is still raw RedCount==0). HARD CONSTRAINT for the builder: acs-verdict.json is written AFTER audit-report.md (1115: 00:15:09 vs 00:13:56; 1117: 01:38:45 vs 01:37:36), so 'have the auditor reconcile against the gate' is structurally impossible without phase reordering or sharing the gating output.
